title: Theophrastus as first draft: the seams with Λ, the Ethics and De anima
description: The First Draft (#1585–#1605) and Aristotelian or Theophrastan (#1583), September 2026, argue Theophrastus's Metaphysics fragment continues Λ, divided from it by name at the hinge where the account passes from complete to needing more. Forecasts state what each seam should show: Λ answering the fragment's aporiai, the Ethics' types containing the Characters' sketches plus the frame, De anima subordinating the De sensibus survey, and HP sharing HA's connectives in a less varied form. #1585 places the fragment after Λ; #1589 refines this, #1597 reopens the direction, and #1671 (October) keeps the seam but calls the order undecidable. The theses argue the Theophrastan function is one operation at two scales, and the you of the Elenchi is the I of the fragment; the corpus contains its own reception.

statements.quote: At this seam the draft is not the draft *before* the treatise; it is the draft *after* it — the working notebook of the treatise's next pass, which never became a treatise. The draft state is confirmed (unresolved, aporetic, method-first); its position in the method's order is reversed from §3.3's prediction: Λ 6–8 → fragment → (the Λ 10 that would answer it, which does not exist).

The fragment is a Β written *after* Λ — the aporiai of the treatise's own unresolved edge, gathered as a whole work, in Β's register (§8.1), with Λ's vocabulary (§8.2), and without Λ's two signature formulae because it is not restating the achieved part but working the unfinished one.

The fragment is a Β written *after* Λ — the aporiai of the treatise's own unresolved edge, gathered as a whole work, in Β's register (§8.1), with Λ's vocabulary (§8.2), and without Λ's two signature formulae because it is not restating the achieved part but working the unfinished one.

**The whole demand-cluster stands in Chapter II, at 5 a 14 – 5 b 10.** Not in Chapter VI, not at 8 a 21, where an earlier misreference put it — a hundred lines earlier than reported, and **before** the perception passage at 7 b 19-22 rather than after it. So the fragment issues its specification, refuses the astronomers' method, and draws the consequence that the first is not the cause of the best, all within its own second chapter, in about seventy lines.

That is not a pupil working through a master's book and objecting as he goes. It is a specification stated early, compactly, and once.

claims.statement: The Theophrastan function's two showings — the *Characters* (reduce embodied material to a registry before theory) and the *Metaphysics* fragment (reopen a sealed architecture into questions after theory) — are one operation at two scales: **from formed object back to examinable constituents.** That is why the same function stands at both edges of the treatise (notebook §10–12), and why "first draft" describes a state and not a position.

statements.quote: The Theophrastan function's two showings — the *Characters* (reduce embodied material to a registry before theory) and the *Metaphysics* fragment (reopen a sealed architecture into questions after theory) — are one operation at two scales: **from formed object back to examinable constituents.** That is why the same function stands at both edges of the treatise (notebook §10–12), and why "first draft" describes a state and not a position.

The Theophrastan texts are drafts on *both* edges of the Aristotelian treatise: before it, where operations are collected but not yet parts (sketches, surveys); after it, where the treatise's own closing aporiai are taken up as the whole work. "First draft of Aristotle" survives as a description of *state* — the method in its less resolved condition — and fails as a description of *position*, which the seams give one at a time and not uniformly.
